Lexicon Latīnitātis Cotīdiānae
Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

profit noun

financial gain

also make a profit, profits, gain, profitable, at a profit, clear (a profit), net (a profit)

classical

Plaut. Capt. 327: damnum praestet facere quam lucrum
Traupman 365: lucrum facere, make a profit

1lucrum: short u (Traupman lūcrum; Lewis & Short marks the u both long and short). De Vaan 349, s.v. lucrum: short *lu- is regular from pretonic *lh₂u-. Hor. C. 1.9.14, quem fors diērum cumque dabit, lucrō, puts lu- in a short place of the Alcaic line, where a long vowel could not stand.

lucrum1, lucrī n.

noun, second declension

profit, gain

To make a profit, lucrum facere or lucrī facere; to make a loss, damnum facere.

Other words

  • quaestus, quaestūs m. — gain, earnings

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Publ. N 5: nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere

    Gain made by work or business; also the business itself (see industry).

  • compendium, compendiī n. — a saving; gain

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.6: cum quaestū compendiōque (Lewis & Short)

    Properly gain made by saving (Lewis & Short).

  • dētergeō, dētergēre, dētersī, dētersum — wipe off, clear (a table); not “clear a profit”

    verb, second conjugation · avoid · classical · Traupman 292

    Traupman: prīmō annō mīlle dollarōs dētergēre, to clear $1000 in the first year. Lewis & Short gives “to wipe off, clean”, and in comedy mēnsam dētergēre, to clear a table (Plaut. Men. 1.1.2), but not the sense of a net gain; we have found no classical instance of it. Making a profit is lucrum facere, or lucrī facere (Cic. Flac. 91).

Examples

  • est etiam ubi profectō damnum praestet facere quam lucrum

    there are times when it is really better to make a loss than a profitPlaut. Capt. 327

  • namque ista subita mē jubet benignitās vigilāre, faciās nē meā culpā lucrum

    this sudden kindness tells me to stay awake, so that you don’t make a profit through my faultPhaedr. 1.23.7–8

  • Nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere.

    No profit is as safe as saving what you have.Publ. N 5

  • lucrum facere

    to make a profitPlaut. Capt. 2.2.77 (Lewis & Short s.v. lucrum)

See also income, business, interest.
